reading.text:
Reading (locked before any Lean): spec thm_cwp, Theorem 3.5, clause "existence and uniqueness"
(on every finite horizon; full tuple law incl. U-law; arbitrary sigma-finite activity; expected
G-monotonicity).

Paper content. For every horizon T>0, under Assumptions 2.2-2.5, system (1.1) admits a solution
Theta = (X,Y,Z,U) in HH, unique (by Thm 3.3), and depending continuously on coefficients/data in
the sense of (3.1) (that last part is Thm 3.1, a separate clause).

A faithful formal statement must contain:
- Setting: arbitrary T>0, arbitrary n, m, d >= 1, arbitrary countably generated (E, calE) with
  arbitrary sigma-finite nu (infinite activity allowed), arbitrary standing basis (usual
  conditions, d-dim Brownian W, independent PRM N with intensity dt nu, filtration the
  augmentation generated by W, N and an independent F_0) - none of these specialised.
- Data: deterministic, jointly Borel coefficients b, sigma, h (Borel into L2(nu;R^n) as in (2.3)),
  f on [0,T] x H x P_2(H), g on R^n x P_2(R^n); xi_0 in L2(Omega, F_0; R^n).
- Hypotheses exactly Assumptions 2.2 (xi_0 in L2, origin values in L2(0,T)), 2.3 (diagonal
  Lipschitz, a.e. t, a.s.; terminal Lipschitz for all X_T, X'_T in L2(F_T)), 2.4 (G full rank),
  2.5 (terminal and interior expected monotonicity along diagonal pairs, the constant
  constraints alpha,beta1,beta2>=0, alpha+beta1>0, beta1+beta2>0, beta1>0 if m<n, alpha,beta2>0 if
  m>n). No extra hypothesis (no finite nu, no pointwise monotonicity, no smallness, no extra
  regularity in t).
- Conclusion: existence of Theta in HH (X, Y cadlag adapted with E sup^2 finite; Z, U predictable
  square integrable) solving (1.1): for every t a.s. X_t = xi_0 + int_0^t b(s,Theta_s,mu_s) ds +
  int_0^t sigma dW + int_0^t int_E h(s,Theta_s^-,e,mu_s^-) Ntilde(ds,de); Y_t = g(X_T, Law X_T) +
  int_t^T f ds - int_t^T Z dW - int_t^T int_E U Ntilde; mu_t = Law(Theta_t), mu_t^- =
  Law(Theta_t^-) (Borel representatives, a.e.-t agreement), with genuine Ito and compensated
  Poisson integrals; and uniqueness: any two solutions in HH are equal in HH (indistinguishable
  X, Y; Z, U a.e.). Formally "exists unique up to the HH identification".
- Watch: the solution notion must not be satisfiable by junk (e.g. stochastic integrals of
  non-square-integrable integrands defaulting to 0, Bochner integrals defaulting to 0, laws of
  non-measurable maps); uniqueness must be in HH (or broader in Hweak) not in a smaller class;
  "unique" should be in the sense of the HH equivalence classes.
- A witness should exhibit a system the paper intends (e.g. Example 5.1(i)) satisfying 2.2-2.5.

comparison.text:
Comparison: spec thm_cwp (Sec3.lean:119-147) against my locked reading.

Setting: arbitrary Omega, G0 independent of the driver, (E, calE) countably generated, nu
sigma-finite (infinite activity allowed), n, m, d > 0, Levy driver, standing filtration
enlJoint, any T > 0. Matches.

Hypotheses: JointBorel T C ((2.3), standing joint Borel measurability, h into L2(nu));
Assumption22 (xi0 strongly F_0-measurable, in L2; origin values b, sigma, h, f at (t, 0, delta_0)
in L2(0,T)); Assumption23 with L (L >= 0; interior a.e. t, all diagonal pairs, a.s., with the
Hilbert-norm W2 on P2(H); terminal for all F_T-measurable L2 X_T, X'_T with W2 on P2(R^n));
G.rank = min m n (full rank, Assumption 2.4; c_G, ||G|| are derived quantities); Assumption25
(terminal, interior a.e. t, admissible constants alpha, beta1, beta2 >= 0, alpha+beta1 > 0,
beta1+beta2 > 0, beta1 > 0 if m < n, alpha, beta2 > 0 if m > n). The Lean Assumption 2.5 demands
integrability of the two pairings; under Assumption 2.3 on L2 diagonal inputs these are integrable,
so this is no extra restriction. Nothing else is assumed.

Conclusion: (existence) some (X, Y, Z, U) with Solution, i.e. PaperSolution over enlJoint for some
representative gamma of h(s, Theta^-_s, ., mu^-_s), with every path cadlag on [0,T]; (uniqueness)
any two Solutions have X, Y indistinguishable on [0,T] and zero energy of the Z- and U-differences
(equality in HH). Matches "admits a solution in HH, unique".

Solution notion (PaperSolution): X, Y adapted on [0,T], every path right-continuous on [0,T),
left limits, E sup |.|^2 finite (S^2); Z predictable, U marked predictable, finite energy, vanishing
off [0,T] (H^2_W, H^2_N); both identities of (1.1) a.s. simultaneously for all t in [0,T] (the
paper's "a.s. for every t", equivalent by the one-null-set remark), with genuine library integrals
(cadlag version of the multidimensional Ito integral, cadlag compensated Poisson integral), the
coefficients evaluated at the tuple Theta_s and its law lawP2 P Theta_s (the paper's Borel
representative mu_s agrees with it a.e. s, and only dt-integrals see it), h at the predictable
tuple of left limits and its law, terminal g(X_T, Law X_T). The fields b_sq, sigma_sq, f_sq,
gamma_sq (finite energy of the coefficient processes) and the measurability fields are consequences
of Assumptions 2.2-2.3 and (2.3) for any paper solution in HH ((2.16)), so the uniqueness half loses
no paper solution and the existence half is at least as strong as the paper's. Junk values: lawP2
is delta_0 off L2, which happens only on a null set of times for a tuple in HH; uLift is 0 off
L2(nu), only on a dt x dP-null set; the integrals are taken only with their integrability
certificates, so no junk enters.

Witness thm_cwp_hypotheses: Example 5.1(i) (nu = delta_0, n = m = d = 1, T = 1, beta1 = beta2 = 1)
satisfies all hypotheses: not vacuous.

Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. The law flow is the exact law lawP2 P Theta_s at every time (Dirac at 0 off L2), not a Borel
   representative; they agree for a.e. s and enter only dt-integrals and dt x dP-a.e.
   evaluations (Lemma A.1).
2. The solution predicate carries the measurability and finite-energy conditions of the coefficient
   processes along Theta and of the jump representative gamma (marked progressive, the paper's being
   predictable: gamma represents a predictable process a.e., so the L2 Poisson integral is the same).
   For a paper solution in HH these follow from (2.3) and Assumptions 2.2-2.3, so neither half of
   the statement changes.
3. Cadlag paths: every path right-continuous on [0,T) with left limits on (0,T]; Z, U are normalised
   to vanish off [0,T]; uniqueness is indistinguishability of X, Y on [0,T] and zero energy of the
   Z-, U-differences, i.e. equality in HH.
4. The identities hold on one null set for all t (equivalent to "a.s. for every t" by right
   continuity, sec3_one_null_set), with a cadlag version of the Ito integral.
5. Assumption 2.5 in Lean demands integrability of its pairings, automatic under Assumption 2.3; H
   carries the max norm but W2 in Assumption 2.3 is the Hilbert-norm W2 (w2H), as printed; full
   rank is G.rank = min m n.

author_review.disagreements:
Labelling only. The review records "faithful" and I record "faithful with representation
choices". The conclusion is the same, and the difference is that I list the encodings of the
solution notion explicitly: the law flow is lawP2 at every time rather than a Borel
representative, the integrability and measurability fields along Theta follow from Assumptions
2.2-2.3, gamma is a marked progressive representative, every path is cadlag, Z and U vanish off
[0,T], the identities hold on one null set for all t, and Assumption 2.5 demands integrable
pairings. None of these changes the statement.
